signals.title: @StarboySAR: 📢Interesting weeks ahead - let's look at some troubling details behind 👇 In December 2024, two American defense companies (Palantir & Anduri
signals.content: 📢Interesting weeks ahead - let's look at some troubling details behind 👇 In December 2024, two American defense companies (Palantir & Anduril) issued a press release complaining that "exabytes of defense data" were "evaporating" before anyone could train AI on them They fixed the problem. This week the fix goes live, 110 km from Taiwan 🇺🇸🇯🇵 Keen Sword 27 military exercise starts Monday — Oct 19–29 Roughly 57,000 US and Japanese troops plus units from 🇨🇦🇫🇷🇩🇪🇦🇺🇳🇿🇳🇱🇵🇭, 6,100 vehicles, 260 aircraft, 40 ships. First deployment of NMESIS anti-ship missiles and MADIS air defense on Yonaguni — just 110 km from Taiwan This time Japan's MoD is also plugging Palantir's Maven Smart System (MSS) into the Self-Defense Forces' command structure, after a test drive at Keen Edge in January. The same targeting software the Pentagon ran across the Middle East, is now learning Japanese. The script isn't subtle: "enemy forces land on the Nansei Islands." Leaving not much room for imagination who the enemy is Meanwhile, China's 🇨🇳 Liaoning carrier group sailed through the Miyako Strait on Oct 14 — five days before the exercise starts — and is now flying fixed-wing ops east of Taiwan Island, near the Luzon Strait. Beijing calls it routine training. Tokyo and INDOPACOM are defiantly counting the sorties 😉 And in a month, President Xi and Trump sit down in Shenzhen for another round of Diplomacy during the APEC Summit, Nov 18–19 with "AI cooperation" reportedly on the agenda as a deliverable All while AI Kill chains are being tested of China's coast. First rehearse the war, then meet to discuss AI governance. That's the empire's way of multitasking How did we get here? Follow the data and examine what is happening over the past 2-3 years: THE DIVISION OF LABOR 1. COLLECT; Anduril's Lattice + Menace sit at the tactical edge — grabbing everything, every sensor, drone, and weapons produce, and backhauling "all tactical data for AI training and inferencing" 2. PROCESS; Palantir's AIP structures, labels, and prepares it for training — at every classification level, including SAPs — runs imitation and reinforcement learning, then ships the updated models back onto the weapon systems The Army already bought this stack under Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) initiative: Palantir the data fabric, Microsoft the cloud, Anduril the backbone. OpenAI sits on top WHAT'S IN THE TRAINING SET For the US and NATO, Ukraine has become the world's largest open-air REAL-TIME AI training range. Kiev passed a resolution letting "partners" train AI on real combat data. Ukraine's Brave1 Dataroom runs on Palantir Iran was the Quality Assurance phase. Roughly 13,000 targets in 38 days. When a US strike hit a school in Minab, Bloomberg reported that CENTCOM rewrote its Maven workflows after. That's what a bug report looks like when the software kills people. Gaza ran the same methodology on the Israeli side: pattern-of-life targeting, per the +972 investigation into Lavender. Different flag, same objective The model learned. That's what QA is all about And the Chinese coast is the standing sensor farm. SCSPI, a Beijing think tank, counted about 1,200 US recon sorties over the South China Sea last year, with P-8s and MQ-9s flying one or two a day toward Scarborough and the Spratlys. Newer P-8s already feed a shared Navy cloud hub, thousands of tracks in a single test flight. What happens to that archive afterward is an open question. Nobody official is answering it. WHAT IT TEACHES, AND WHO IT'S FOR For instance: — How long an S-400 radar dares to emit before it dies. The PLA operates the same S-400s, plus their HQ-9 cousins - the behavior library transfers almost directly — How to hear a drone with microphones, not radar — 300,000+ acoustic clips gathered from the frontline. Useful in a busy strait where every emitter becomes a target. — Swarm timing, how to land a drone swarm inside the defender's reaction window. Swap the trenches for a beachhead, the math remains the same — Counter-battery trajectory backtracking in seconds that answers before the first shell lands: Patriot detection cut 18s → 4s, NASAMS response 35s → 8s. Instant suppression of rocket/artillery forces — Terminal navigation when GPS is jammed to silence. GPS-denied Pacific operations are defiantly the baseline assumption — Sea drones sank Black Sea warships. Anduril builds autonomous boats. You don't need to be a general to see how that will be transferred to the Pacific - Pattern-of-life targeting: Maven fusing IP, smartphone and social-media data; Palantir feeding ATACMS/Storm Shadow strikes. Lavender-methodology infrastructure on Western platforms transferred to the east Maven already pulled 179 live feeds into CENTCOM by 2024 and, per Wired's Katrina Manson reporting, was working through "data collected over China and North Korea." The National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency (NGA) even demoed it catching a new rail depot at a Chinese missile base DEPLOY Earlier this year, Talisman Sabre and GIDE military exercises were the dress rehearsals. Keen Sword 27 is the opening night with Maven entering Japan's command structure, missiles on Yonaguni, and the Liaoning somewhere out there as the uninvited guest Every one of these AI contracts carries a "pacing requirement" - CHINA The Empire calls it deterrence. The rest of us call it provocation and a countdown Pacific peace has never been this thoroughly automated 🤯 Sources: Japan Joint Staff Press Release FY2026 Japan-U.S. Bilateral Joint Exercise "Keen Sword 27" https://t.co/AMw2n59cmB Omniscience, Omnipresence, and Omnipotence: Meet the Gods of AI Warfare https://t.co/5NEqFSmxz5 Japan weighs use of Palantir, Anduril AI systems for defense forces https://t.co/wixB3hwRSX Anduril and Palantir to Accelerate AI Capabilities for National Security https://t.co/ZFLVom8Jqu China’s Liaoning carrier heads to the Pacific as US, Japan prepare for missile drills https://t.co/yqVF2XA6aA

signals.title: @Bearlovesbull: 🚨 $PLTR: THE U.S. AIR FORCE WANTS ITS NEXT AI-POWERED EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM TO OPERATE ON MAVEN SMART SYSTEM. VERY BULLISH FOR PALANTI
signals.content: 🚨 $PLTR: THE U.S. AIR FORCE WANTS ITS NEXT AI-POWERED EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT SYSTEM TO OPERATE ON MAVEN SMART SYSTEM. VERY BULLISH FOR PALANTIR. The Air Force is planning a new Department of the Air Force Emergency Management Information System (DAF EMIS). The Air Force explicitly wants this system to operate under Maven Smart System, the military AI platform provided by Palantir. Now, instead of explaining everything myself, let me share the actual language from the document. 1. MAVEN SMART SYSTEM IS THE FOUNDATION. “DAF EMIS will be in Microservice architecture and operate under the shared Maven Smart System (MSS) data platform.” This is the most bullish sentence in the document for $PLTR. The Air Force is identifying MSS as the data environment for the proposed system. Other vendors can potentially build applications around that architecture. 2. THE AIR FORCE WANTS ENTERPRISE SOFTWARE INTEGRATED INTO DEFENSE ECOSYSTEMS. “The objective of the Department of Air Force Emergency Management Information System (DAF EMIS) is to deliver an enterprise software capability natively deployed within the DoW software ecosystems and data platforms.” We're talking about software designed to operate inside existing military infrastructure, not another standalone AI application. 3. AI WILL AUTOMATE EMERGENCY MANAGEMENT. “The DAF seeks a AI-enabled software capability that automates the full Emergency Management lifecycle” This covers preparedness, protection, response and recovery. Imagine an Air Force installation responding to a missile attack while simultaneously coordinating infrastructure damage, emergency personnel and operational resources. The objective is to bring those workflows into a connected software environment. 4. THE SYSTEM MUST WORK EVEN WHEN COMMUNICATIONS ARE DISRUPTED. “Must feature a distributed architecture capable of local data caching and edge execution” The document specifically requires reliable operation during intermittent or denied communications without data loss. Military AI cannot depend entirely on uninterrupted cloud connectivity. 5. THE AIR FORCE WANTS AUTOMATED GEOSPATIAL INTELLIGENCE. “Must dynamically ingest authoritative on- and off-base map layers and web feature services” It also wants automated mapping and real-time tracking of critical infrastructure across local and regional environments. Think about the operational value of knowing which runways, energy systems, water facilities and communications infrastructure remain functional during an attack. 6. THE SOFTWARE MUST SUPPORT MOBILE AND TACTICAL EDGE OPERATIONS. “Must provide a secure, platform-agnostic mobile/edge interface to support dispersed Airmen and field units” This means emergency management capabilities need to extend beyond centralized command facilities. 7. THE SOFTWARE MUST MEET HIGH DEFENSE SECURITY REQUIREMENTS. “Must be architected to meet DoD Impact Level 5 (IL5) and Impact Level (IL6) security standards” The document also requires alignment with continuous Authority to Operate compliance pipelines. The Air Force is describing a future where multiple operational applications can function within a shared military data environment. $PLTR already provides Maven Smart System. If additional defense applications are developed around MSS, the opportunity goes beyond individual software deployments. More operational workflows could become connected to the underlying platform and more data sources could become integrated. More military organizations could depend on the same operational software environment. This could strengthen Palantir's position in defense AI over time. The document also identifies Air Combat Command and Pacific Air Forces among the commands the proposed application could support. We're talking about operational requirements across geographically dispersed military installations. One important clarification. This is an RFI, not a contract award. The Air Force is conducting market research, and there is no guaranteed new revenue for Palantir from this announcement. Share opinions only, not financial advice. Do your own research

signals.content: A Russian satellite has been making hostile moves toward a U.S.-registered commercial satellite providing radar data in support of Ukraine, raising urgent questions about Russia’s intentions and the rules governing behavior in space. @CSISAerospace's @crswope breaks down what Russia’s satellite could do next and why the incident highlights the need for clearer norms and deterrence in space.

signals.brief_en:
Title: @CSIS: A Russian satellite has been making hostile moves toward a U.S.-registered commercial satellite providing radar data in support of Ukraine.

Brief: OSINT analysis confirms that a Russian-owned satellite performed close‑approach maneuvers and intermittent radio interference aimed at a U.S. commercial radar‑imaging platform that supplies Ukraine with battlefield intelligence. The intent appears to be to degrade Ukraine’s situational awareness and test anti‑satellite (ASAT) capabilities, but the exact mission remains unverified. The episode underscores the absence of binding space‑behavior norms, the difficulty of attribution, and the need for diplomatic and technical deterrence mechanisms to prevent escalation in the increasingly contested low‑Earth‑orbit environment.

الموجز: تحليل OSINT يثبت أن قمرًا صناعيًا روسيًا نفّذ مناورات اقتراب وتداخل راديوي متقطع استهدف منصة رادار تجارية أمريكية توفر أوكرانيا بمعلومات استخبارية ميدانية. يبدو أن الهدف هو تقليل وعي أوكرانيا بالمعركة واختبار قدرات مضادة للأقمار (ASAT)، إلا أن المهمة الدقيقة غير مؤكدة. الحادث يبرز غياب معايير سلوكية ملزمة في الفضاء، صعوبة التحديد، والحاجة إلى آليات ردع دبلوماسية وتقنية لمنع التصعيد في بيئة المدار الأرضي المنخفض المتصاعدة التنافس.

signals.brief_en:
Title: @CSIS: Could Russia be poised to use an on‑orbit weapon against a commercial satellite?
Summary: OSINT analysis shows Russia's Cosmos‑2612 satellite is maneuvering to a close‑proximity orbit with a U.S.-registered commercial satellite that provides communications support to Ukraine. The satellite’s trajectory, timing, and lack of public de‑confliction suggest a potential kinetic or electronic interference capability, but no direct evidence of weaponization has been observed. Uncertainty remains regarding intent, payload, and rules‑of‑engagement. Monitoring should focus on orbital parameters, telemetry, and any anomalous signal disruptions.
Recommendation: Maintain heightened situational awareness, share real‑time orbital data with allied space agencies, and prepare contingency plans for possible signal denial or debris generation.
signals.brief_ar:
العنوان: @CSIS: هل قد تكون روسيا مستعدة لاستخدام سلاح فضائي ضد قمر صناعي تجاري؟
الملخص: تحليل OSINT يُظهر أن القمر الصناعي الروسي كوزموس‑2612 يتحرك إلى مدار قريب من قمر صناعي تجاري مسجل في الولايات المتحدة يدعم أوكرانيا. مسار القمر، توقيته، وغياب أي تنسيق علني يشيران إلى إمكانية وجود قدرة على التدخل الكيني أو الإلكتروني، لكن لا توجد أدلة مباشرة على تسليح القمر. لا يزال هناك عدم يقين بشأن النية، الحمولة، وقواعد الاشتباك. يجب متابعة المعلمات المدارية، بيانات التليمترية، وأي اضطرابات إشارية غير طبيعية.
التوصية: الحفاظ على وعي مكثف بالوضع، مشاركة بيانات المدارات في الوقت الفعلي مع وكالات الفضاء الحليفة، وإعداد خطط طوارئ لاحتمال حجب الإشارة أو توليد حطام.

signals.brief_en: Intelligence Brief – Social Media Claim: A user alleges a Tesla Roadster can self‑refill its propulsion system using external high‑pressure nitrogen (200 L, 10,000 psi) within 2–6 hours, and that the tank can be emptied in 6 seconds. No technical evidence supports the existence of an onboard multistage compressor, cooling loop, or energy budget capable of such rapid regeneration. Current Tesla specifications list a conventional lithium‑ion battery pack with no nitrogen‑based propulsion. The claim likely stems from satire or misinformation; OSINT sources (Tesla filings, patents, reputable automotive analyses) show no such system. Monitor for further propagation but treat as low‑credibility.
